facts.raw_span: A 13-year-old boy with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia
receiving maintenance therapy (daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone)
3 months of hematochezia
two to three loose bowel movements per day (Bristol type 5–6) with mixed blood
polyethylene glycol produced looser stools without reducing bleeding
denied abdominal pain, weight loss, rashes, arthritis, oral or perianal lesions
intermittently neutropenic and consistently lymphopenic
abdomen was soft and nontender
a small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted
Stool studies, including culture and PCR for Clostridioides difficile, cytomegalovirus, and adenovirus, were negative
Colonoscopy showed multiple semisessile, nonbleeding 1–5 mm polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa
histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains

concepts.why: The patient presented with 3 months of hematochezia and two to three loose bowel movements per day with mixed blood.
The patient was intermittently neutropenic and had colonoscopy findings of multiple semisessile, nonbleeding polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa.
The patient was receiving maintenance therapy with daily 6-mercaptopurine, weekly methotrexate, monthly vincristine and dexamethasone, which can cause colitis.
The histiocytes contained numerous basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains.
The patient was diagnosed with T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia.
A small nonbleeding external hemorrhoid was noted on examination.
The patient had colonoscopy findings of multiple semisessile, nonbleeding polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa.
The patient was consistently lymphopenic and had colonoscopy findings of multiple semisessile, nonbleeding polyps in the rectum and sigmoid colon with surrounding erythematous, eroded mucosa.

The presence of basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions in histiocytes that are strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid-Schiff stains explains the uncovered fact of negative stool studies for common pathogens.

rationales.F01: T-cell lymphoblastic leukemia is a known risk factor for gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F02: Chemotherapy is a known risk factor for neutropenic colitis and chemotherapy-induced colitis.
rationales.F03: Hematochezia is a common symptom of gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F04: Loose bowel movements with mixed blood are consistent with gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F09: A nonbleeding external hemorrhoid can cause gastrointestinal bleeding.
rationales.F10: Negative stool studies make infectious colitis less likely.
rationales.F11: Colonoscopy findings are consistent with inflammatory bowel disease and immune-mediated colitis.
rationales.F12: Histiocytic infiltration with basophilic inclusions is characteristic of malakoplakia.

frontier_selector.rationale: The presence of histiocytes with basophilic spherical and targetoid inclusions that were strongly positive on von Kossa and periodic acid–Schiff stains is highly suggestive of Malakoplakia, which explains the decisive findings without strong contradiction.
